pull.title: feat(harnesses): serve Kimi Code from a config.toml MCC owns, named by the flag Kimi publishes
pull.body:
## What this adds

One harness: **Kimi Code**, Moonshot's `kimi` CLI. Registry id `kimi_code`, binary `kimi` (alias `kimi-cli`), launcher `mcc-kimi`, protocol Anthropic Messages, catalogue format `kimi`, `rtk_agent=False`. Version **6.28.0** (MINOR), `uv lock` in the same commit.

It is a **Python tool on PyPI**, not an npm package: `uv tool install kimi-cli`, or `pipx install kimi-cli`. MCC installs neither — the registry's hint is printed and the launcher exits 127.

## What the spec said, and what the installed package actually does

Everything below was read out of the installed package's own source at **1.50.0**, not out of the vendor's docs. Four of the spec's assumptions do not hold, and each one changed the design.

| The spec / the docs | Kimi Code 1.50.0, in its own source |
| --- | --- |
| `KIMI_CODE_HOME` overrides the config directory | **No such variable.** The string does not occur in the package. `kimi_cli/share.py:get_share_dir()` is `$KIMI_SHARE_DIR` or `~/.kimi`; the config is `<share dir>/config.toml` (`kimi_cli/config.py:get_config_file`). `~/.kimi-code/` is an older layout — this machine still has one, last written 2026-07-20, and it was not touched. |
| `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` | `~/.kimi/config.toml` |
| `[models."…"]` carries `max_output_size` | **No such field.** `LLMModel` is `provider`, `model`, `max_context_size`, `capabilities`, `display_name`. Kimi derives the completion cap itself in `kimi_cli/llm.py:compute_max_completion_tokens`. |
| `capabilities` ← vision / tools / reasoning | `ModelCapability = Literal["image_in", "video_in", "thinking", "always_thinking"]`. **No tools capability, and no per-model reasoning-effort field anywhere in the schema.** |
| `[providers.*]` vs `KIMI_MODEL_*` precedence is contradictory — UNCONFIRMED | **Settled.** `kimi_cli/llm.py:augment_provider_with_env_vars` overrides `base_url`/`api_key`/model fields only for provider types `kimi`, `openai_legacy`, `openai_responses`. An `anthropic` provider — the only type that reaches MCC — falls through its `case _: pass`. For the type MCC uses there is no precedence, because there is no override. |

Also confirmed from source: `create_llm`'s `case "anthropic"` builds `kosong.contrib.chat_provider.anthropic.Anthropic`, which is the **official `anthropic` SDK**, so the header on the wire is `x-api-key` — the one `require_proxy_auth` learned to read in #245.

## Config delivery: `--config-file`, not a merge, not the share dir

Kimi publishes `kimi --config-file PATH`. So MCC writes `~/.fcc/kimi-code-config.toml` and passes that path. **`~/.kimi/config.toml` is never read, written or backed up** — no TOML merge writer was needed at all.

`KIMI_SHARE_DIR` existed and was **deliberately not used**: that directory also holds the user's sessions, OAuth credentials, plugins and background-worker state, so redirecting it to serve one config file would hide every session they have. The flag moves the config alone.

The flag goes **ahead** of the user's arguments, because it binds to Kimi's root Typer callback: `kimi term --config-file X` would be read as an argument to `term`.

**The trade is stated, not hidden** — in `README`, `docs/USAGE.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and on the card: `--config-file` *replaces* the config document rather than overlaying it (`cli/__init__.py` picks one of `--config`, `--config-file`, the default path; `load_config` reads that one file). So an `mcc-kimi` session takes Kimi's own defaults for `theme`, `hooks` and `loop_control`. Sessions, skills and MCP servers come from the share dir and from Kimi's own MCP defaults and are unaffected.

## The one deviation from the brief: the token is in MCC's own file

The brief said to keep the proxy token off disk, and to stop rather than write it if the CLI supports no reference form. **Kimi supports none**, and the evidence is in the table above: `api_key` is a plain `SecretStr` with no `"$VAR"` / `"{env:VAR}"` / `"!command"` form, and the environment overrides do not reach an `anthropic` provider. There is no out-of-band channel; the choice was a literal value or no Kimi Code support.

It writes the literal, into a file **MCC owns** under `~/.fcc`, `chmod 0600` (best-effort; close to a no-op on Windows), in the same directory as the `~/.fcc/.env` that already stores the identical `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in clear. Nothing is disclosed that was not disclosed already, and **nothing is written into a document the user owns**. With proxy auth off the value is the existing `fcc-no-auth` marker, which is not a credential. Flagged under Residual risks.

## Serialiser

`application/catalogues/kimi.py`, pure `Iterable[CatalogueModel] -> (document, DefaultedFields)`:

| Ladder | Kimi |
| --- | --- |
| `context_length` | `max_context_size` |
| `max_output_tokens` | *(no field — Kimi derives it)*, and **not** recorded as defaulted: a field the CLI does not have is not a field the CLI guessed |
| `supports_vision` | `capabilities: ["image_in"]` |
| `supports_tool_calls` | *(no field)* |
| `reasoning.can_reason` | `capabilities: ["thinking"]` |
| `reasoning.mandatory` | `capabilities: ["always_thinking"]` |
| effort rungs | *(no field — `clamp_efforts` is deliberately not called)* |
| prices, pinned params | *(no fields)* |

`MODEL_ENTRY_PATHS["kimi"] = ("models",)` — a third shape, a mapping at the document root, because that is what `Config.models` is.

**Unknown stays unknown, argued rather than asserted.** `max_context_size` is a *required* int, so an unknown one cannot be omitted — and MCC still refuses to invent a window. It writes `0`, which is Kimi's own marker: `compute_max_completion_tokens` branches on `max_context_size <= 0` and falls back to its own 32,000-token budget. The AST guard covers `kimi.py` (glob) and passes; `test_a_fully_unknown_model_never_produces_a_zero_limit` now derives its zero exemption from each format's declared `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` rather than from a hard-coded list, so a stray zero anywhere else in any format still fails.

A real generated fragment, from the scratch proxy:

```toml
[providers.mcc]
type = "anthropic"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8199"
api_key = "fcc-no-auth"

[models."mcc/custom_scratch/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"]
provider = "mcc"
model = "custom_scratch/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"
max_context_size = 200000
capabilities = ["image_in", "thinking"]
display_name = "custom_scratch/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"

[models."mcc/custom_scratch/acme/quiet-1"]
provider = "mcc"
model = "custom_scratch/acme/quiet-1"
max_context_size = 0
display_name = "custom_scratch/acme/quiet-1"

[_mcc_defaulted]
"mcc/custom_scratch/acme/quiet-1" = ["max_context_size", "capabilities.image_in", "capabilities.thinking"]
```

The first model's `200000` is the ladder's resolved answer; the second is the unknown case, written as Kimi's own `0` and recorded.

## New: an atomic TOML writer

Kimi's `config.toml` is the first generated catalogue that is not JSON, so `config/harness_toml.py` gives it the same atomic write-if-changed contract `config/atomic_json.py` gives the others, over a deterministic emitter narrow enough to **raise** on anything it cannot encode. `tomllib` reads TOML and does not write it; a silently mis-encoded config is a model picker that is empty for reasons nobody can see. `HarnessCatalogue.document_format` selects the writer in the launcher and in the fan-out publisher; `admin_harness_routes._read_catalogue` selects the parser.

## One bug this found, by launching rather than by reasoning

The first real launch logged `POST /v1/v1/messages 404`. Kimi's client is the **official** Anthropic SDK, whose route is already `/v1/messages`; the OpenCode family and Command Code go through Vercel's `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, which appends a bare `/messages` and does want the `/v1`. So the correct base URL for Kimi is the exact opposite of the correct base URL for them. `kimi_base_url` now strips a trailing `/v1` instead of appending one, and the second commit says why in the place a reader would otherwise "fix" it back.

## Real launch proof

Scratch MCC on **127.0.0.1:8199** with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` redirected under the scratchpad, a fake gateway on 8299, a custom provider `custom_scratch`, and a seeded models.dev cache. The live 8082 install was not touched.

```
$ mcc-kimi --print --output-format text -p "say MCC-KIMI-OK" \
      -m mcc/custom_scratch/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
My Claude Code: 1 model(s) publish no value for one or more fields, so Kimi Code falls back to its own default:
  mcc/custom_scratch/acme/quiet-1: max_context_size, capabilities.image_in, capabilities.thinking
say MCC-KIMI-OK
TurnBegin(user_input='say MCC-KIMI-OK')
StepBegin(n=1)
TextPart(type='text', text='MCC-KIMI-OK')
StatusUpdate(
    context_usage=3.5e-05,
    context_tokens=7,
    max_context_tokens=200000,
    ...
)
TurnEnd()
```

```
# scratch server log
INFO:  127.0.0.1:22470 - "POST /v1/messages HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

`max_context_tokens=200000` is the ladder's own number reaching Kimi's status display — Kimi Code publishes **no model-list subcommand**, so this is the only surface it offers for that check.

**Auth**, with `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=scratch-proxy-token` on the scratch proxy:

```
POST /v1/messages, no header      -> 401
POST /v1/messages, x-api-key: ... -> 200
mcc-kimi --print -p "..."         -> 200 OK, prints MCC-KIMI-OK
```

The generated file then carries `api_key = "scratch-proxy-token"` and Kimi's official SDK sends it as `x-api-key`, which `require_proxy_auth` accepts since #245.

**Zero-clobber, verified:** the machine's real `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` still has its 2026-07-20 mtime and was never opened for content; there is no `~/.kimi/config.toml` on it at all.

## Browser drive

Chrome DevTools MCP against `127.0.0.1:8199/admin`. Screenshots in `screenshots-harness-pr6/`.

| # | What | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | Kimi card, server launched **without** the scratch `kimi` on PATH | `Not installed`, with Moonshot's own install line. Honest, no crash. |
| 02 | Kimi card, server launched **with** it on PATH | `Installed`, `binary_path` = the scratch `kimi.EXE`. Detection works. |
| 03 | Coding agents page, full | 6 cards; Kimi Code last. |
| 04 | Guide → *Point another CLI here* | `mcc-kimi` in the command block, with the flag/token paragraph. |
| 05 | Get Started → launcher list | Kimi Code card with its summary and `mcc-kimi`. |

Card meta rows, read out of the live DOM:

```
Protocol      Anthropic Messages (POST /v1/messages)
Catalogue     …\.fcc\kimi-code-config.toml
Last written  2026-09-01T23:22:56Z
Models        2
Config flag   --config-file - passed for this launch only, so your own config file is never edited
CLI defaults  1 model(s) carry a value Kimi Code supplied because no provider published one
```

Command list on the card, every one with a copy button:

```
mcc-kimi
mcc-kimi -m mcc/<provider>/<model>
mcc-kimi --print -p "<prompt>"
mcc-kimi --quiet -p "<prompt>"
mcc-kimi info
```

**Console: zero errors, zero warnings.** (Two pre-existing DevTools *issues* on the page — unlabelled form fields, lazy images without dimensions — neither introduced here.)

## Tests

New:

- `tests/config/test_harness_toml.py` — 9: round-trips through `tomllib`; quotes a slashed model key; scalars never land inside a following table; LF-terminated stable bytes; unchanged document not rewritten; unencodable value raises; credentials resolved only at the placeholders and the source left alone; resolving twice is a no-op; base URL is the proxy root and never carries `/v1`.
- `tests/application/test_kimi_serialiser.py` — 10: provider block; context + wire name; **no output limit and none recorded**; unknown context is Kimi's own `0` and is recorded; capabilities use Kimi's vocabulary and only its positives; mandatory thinking → `always_thinking`; a known "no" is an absence, never a default; the no-thinking variant gets no thinking capability; `video_in` never claimed; `model_entries` finds them by the declared path.
- `tests/cli/test_kimi_launcher.py` — 8: flag precedes the user's argv; no config → plain launch; passthrough set incl. `-V` and the deliberate exclusion of `acp`/`term`/`web`; end-to-end written document; the no-auth marker; 0600 best effort; registry states file + flag + format.
- `tests/runtime/test_catalogue_fanout.py` — +2: a TOML catalogue is written as TOML with credentials resolved; never created for an unlaunched harness.
- `tests/api/test_admin_harnesses.py` — +1: a TOML catalogue is read back with the parser its format needs.
- `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` — +1: `test_a_flag_owning_harness_names_the_flag_it_is_pointed_with`.

Updated: `test_every_catalogue_declares_how_it_reaches_its_agent`, `test_a_config_owning_harness_names_the_variable_it_is_pointed_with` (now a variable **or** a flag, with a new assertion that every file-owning harness has one — Codex the stated exception), `test_a_merging_harness_never_also_claims_a_config_variable` (+ `config_flag`), `test_the_default_path_resolves_under_the_fcc_config_directory`, `test_a_fully_unknown_model_never_produces_a_zero_limit`, `test_coding_agents_view_renders_one_card_per_harness` (5 → 6), the installer stub command lists (both copies).

Counts:

- `uv run --offline pytest -q --tb=line` → **8376 passed, 15 failed, 38 skipped**. The 15 are the known local baseline: 6 `tests/websearch/*` + 2 `tests/api/test_web_server_tools.py` (a real Exa key in the developer's environment), 6 `tests/scripts/test_installers.py` PowerShell cases, 1 `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache` — all reproduced on `fork/main` with this branch stashed. `tests/cli/test_desktop_rtk.py::test_checked_reflects_persisted_state` flaked once under xdist and passes with `-n 0`.
- jsdom alone: `uv run --offline pytest -q -n 0 tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` → **187 passed** (186 before, +1 new).
- `ruff format --check` repo-wide, `ruff check src tests`, `ty check` — all clean.

## Docs

`README.md` (Coding agents row, install list, troubleshooting row, a Kimi Code section, the gateway-vs-harness box), `docs/USAGE.md` §6 (a Kimi Code subsection with the four-row "what the docs would have told you" table, the field-mapping table extended with a Kimi column, the `max_context_size = 0` explanation, the gateway-vs-harness box), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (console script, the launcher's paragraph, the TOML writer, the token decision), `index.html` (Get Started card, Guide `#guide-other` block and its paragraph), `mcc-help` and both installer summaries — the last two generated from the registry.

## Residual risks

- **The proxy token is on disk in `~/.fcc/kimi-code-config.toml`.** Justified above and documented in three places, but it *is* a second copy of a value that previously lived only in `~/.fcc/.env`. `chmod 0600` is close to a no-op on Windows. If Kimi ever adds a reference form, this should move to it.
- **`--config-file` replaces rather than overlays**, so `theme`, `hooks` and `loop_control` from the user's own `config.toml` do not apply to an `mcc-kimi` session. Documented; there is no overlay mechanism in 1.50.0 to use instead.
- **No default model.** `Config.default_model` is left empty because MCC publishes no "primary" model and picking one would be inventing a preference. A bare `mcc-kimi` therefore needs `-m` or `/model`. The card, `mcc-help` and the docs all say so.
- **Read against 1.50.0 only.** The five source facts this design rests on are version-pinned observations. `augment_provider_with_env_vars`' `case _: pass` in particular could gain an `anthropic` branch in a later release, which would make the token-on-disk trade unnecessary.
- **`~/.kimi-code/` still exists on machines that used an older build.** MCC neither reads nor migrates it; a user who has one and no `~/.kimi` sees Kimi create the new layout on first run, which is Kimi's behaviour and not MCC's.
- **`video_in` is never emitted.** The ladder resolves no video signal, so every model would be an unknown and recording one per model would bury the two capabilities that matter. If a video signal is added upstream this needs revisiting.
- The end-to-end run used a **fake** gateway on 8299 and a custom provider. The inbound half (`POST /v1/messages`, auth, catalogue, config) is real; the upstream half is not a real vendor.

commit.message:
feat(harnesses): serve Kimi Code from a config.toml MCC owns, named by the flag Kimi publishes

Kimi Code is Moonshot's `kimi` CLI, a Python tool published on PyPI as
`kimi-cli`. Everything below was read out of the installed package's own source
at 1.50.0 rather than out of Moonshot's docs, because four things the docs and
the harness spec would have told you are not true of that build:

* There is no `KIMI_CODE_HOME`. The string does not occur in the package. The
  share directory is `$KIMI_SHARE_DIR` or `~/.kimi` (`kimi_cli/share.py`) and
  the config document is `<share dir>/config.toml`. `~/.kimi-code/` is an older
  layout that a machine can still be carrying.
* `LLMModel` has no `max_output_size`. It is `provider`, `model`,
  `max_context_size`, `capabilities`, `display_name` and nothing else; Kimi
  derives the completion cap itself in `compute_max_completion_tokens`. So the
  ladder's output ceiling has nowhere to go, and is not recorded as defaulted
  either -- a field the CLI does not have is not a field the CLI guessed.
* The capability vocabulary is exactly `image_in`, `video_in`, `thinking`,
  `always_thinking`. There is no tools capability and no per-model
  reasoning-effort field anywhere in the schema, so MCC's effort rungs have no
  counterpart to clamp into and `clamp_efforts` is not called from this
  serialiser.
* `augment_provider_with_env_vars` overrides `api_key` from the environment
  only for provider types `kimi`, `openai_legacy` and `openai_responses`. An
  `anthropic` provider -- the only type that reaches MCC's inbound surface --
  falls through its `case _: pass`. That settles the spec's open question about
  `[providers.*]`-versus-`KIMI_MODEL_*` precedence: for the provider type MCC
  uses, there is no precedence, because there is no override.

The user's `~/.kimi/config.toml` is never read, written or backed up. Kimi
publishes `--config-file PATH`, so this is the first harness pointed at an
MCC-owned document by a command-line flag rather than by an environment
variable, and no TOML merge writer was needed at all. `KIMI_SHARE_DIR` was
available and deliberately not used: that directory also holds the user's
sessions, credentials, plugins and background-worker state, and redirecting it
to serve one config file would hide every session they have. The flag moves the
config alone. It goes ahead of the user's arguments because it binds to Kimi's
root Typer callback and would otherwise be read as an argument to a subcommand.

The trade is stated rather than hidden, in the docs and on the card:
`--config-file` replaces the config document rather than overlaying it, so an
`mcc-kimi` session takes Kimi's own defaults for `theme`, `hooks` and
`loop_control`. Sessions, skills and MCP servers come from elsewhere and are
untouched.

This is the one harness whose generated file carries the proxy token, and the
reason is a property of Kimi's schema rather than a choice. `api_key` is a
plain `SecretStr`: there is no `"$VAR"`, `"{env:VAR}"` or `"!command"`
reference form of the kind Command Code publishes, and the environment
overrides above do not reach an `anthropic` provider. There is no out-of-band
channel, so the alternatives were a literal value or no Kimi Code support. The
literal goes into a file MCC owns under `~/.fcc`, chmod 0600, in the same
directory as the `~/.fcc/.env` that already stores the identical
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in clear -- nothing is disclosed that was not disclosed
already, and nothing is written into a document the user owns. With proxy auth
off the value is the existing `fcc-no-auth` marker, which is not a credential.

Kimi's `config.toml` is also the first generated catalogue that is not JSON.
`config/harness_toml.py` gives it the same atomic write-if-changed contract
`config/atomic_json.py` gives the others, over a deterministic emitter narrow
enough to raise on anything it cannot encode: `tomllib` reads TOML and does not
write it, and a silently mis-encoded config is a model picker that is empty for
reasons nobody can see. `HarnessCatalogue.document_format` selects the writer in
both the launcher and the background fan-out.

`max_context_size` is where "unknown stays unknown" had to be argued rather
than asserted. The field is a required int, so an unknown one cannot be
omitted -- and MCC still refuses to invent a context window. It writes `0`,
which is Kimi's own marker: `compute_max_completion_tokens` branches on
`max_context_size <= 0` and falls back to its own 32,000-token budget. The
serialiser contract test now derives its zero exemption from each format's
declared `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` rather than from a list, so a stray zero
anywhere else in any format still fails the guard.

The harness id is `kimi_code`, deliberately not `kimi`: `kimi` and
`kimi_coding` are upstream Moonshot gateways in `config/provider_catalog.py`,
and `mcc-kimi` needs neither of them switched on. The gateway-vs-harness
paragraph in README and USAGE now names this pair alongside Command Code's.

fix(harnesses): give Kimi Code the proxy root, because its SDK owns the /v1

Measured against a scratch proxy rather than reasoned: `mcc-kimi` logged
`POST /v1/v1/messages 404 Not Found` and the CLI reported a bare
`Error code: 404`, with nothing in either message saying which half of the URL
was doubled.

The cause is that Kimi's client is not the same one every other harness uses.
`kosong.contrib.chat_provider.anthropic.Anthropic` hands `base_url` to
`anthropic.AsyncAnthropic`, the *official* Anthropic SDK, whose message route
is already `/v1/messages`. The OpenCode family and Command Code go through
Vercel's `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, which appends a bare `/messages` and therefore
does want a base URL ending in `/v1` -- so the correct value for Kimi is the
exact opposite of the correct value for them, and the shared helper that
appended `/v1` was wrong here.

`kimi_base_url` now strips any trailing `/v1` instead of appending one, and
says why in the place a reader would otherwise "fix" it back. With that, the
same launch answers 200 and Kimi prints the model's reply.
